text.p: Austrian fibre maker Lenzing on Monday reported a provisional 1996 pretax loss of around 160 million schillings ($13.4 million) and warned that earnings were not expected to improve in the current year.

"The difficulties are posed by the global weakness of textile markets," the group said in a statement. "In view of the current market situation, no improvement of the group's earnings situation can be expected in 1997."
Lenzing last year reported a pretax profit of 312.6 million schillings.
The group said sales fell to "almost" eight billion schillings in 1996, from 8.7 billion a year earlier.

Despite a five percent increase in prices at the start of the year, European fibre prices remained at an "extremely unsatisfactory" level. The U.S. market was dogged by large overcapacities, while prices in Asia were also insufficient, it added.

Lenzing said it would push ahead with its cost savings programme instituted last year, which should help earnings improve in 1998. It said the group's board had yet to decide on the 1996 dividend. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 11.98 Austrian Schillings)
